note: Rewritten from Ahmad 1965, original in English (Termites (Isoptera) of Thailand, Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History 131: 1–113). The holotype and one paratype soldier, together with nymphs, were collected by M. Ahmad on 1962-03-05 from an intact part of a tree stump at Ka-Chong, Thailand. In the key the species is separated from the other species of the genus by the "small papilla-like tubercle at the tip of the frontal projections". Fig. 5 (soldier head and pronotum in dorsal and lateral view, postmentum in ventral view, antenna) is not translated; the nymph is not described.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very close to Glyptotermes concavifrons Krishna et Emerson from western Java and to G. kirbyi Krishna et Emerson from Sumatra. It differs from G. concavifrons in the shorter mandibles with less curvature at the tip, and in the narrower head and pronotum. In G. kirbyi the head is distinctly longer, the tips of the mandibles are more strongly curved and the pronotum is wider.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale reddish brown, slightly darker near the postclypeus; labrum pale brown; the outer three quarters of the mandibles dark brown, the base reddish brown; antennae brownish yellow; pronotum yellow; legs and abdominal tergites brownish yellow. The head bears scattered setae; the frons several short setae; the outer base of the mandibles several short hairs; the pronotum several setae along the lateral margins and a few scattered setae on the disc. The head is elongate with parallel sides, slightly narrowed behind the antennae; the Y-suture is present but indistinct; the frontal projections are distinct and small, each with a papilla-like tubercle at its tip; the frons is concave in profile. The compound eyes are whitish, oval and indistinct. The labrum is small with parallel sides and a broadly rounded anterior margin. The mandibles are long, with a weak basal swelling; the left mandible has 3 marginal teeth, the anterior cutting edge of the first marginal tooth shorter than its posterior cutting edge, and that posterior cutting edge longer than the anterior cutting edge of the second marginal tooth; the right mandible has 2 marginal teeth. The postmentum is elongate and flat, narrowest at the basal third. The antennae have 12 segments; segment 2 slightly longer than segment 3 and segment 4 slightly longer than segment 3. The pronotum is narrower than the head; its anterior margin shallowly concave, the sides convex, the middle of the posterior margin slightly concave. Measurements (mm, holotype and paratype soldiers respectively): head length to the lateral base of the mandibles 1.85, 1.75; head width 1.17, 1.20; length of the left mandible 0.95, —; distance from the first marginal tooth of the left mandible to the tip of the apical tooth 0.25, —; length of the right mandible 0.95, 1.00; distance from the first marginal tooth of the right mandible to the tip of the apical tooth 0.40, 0.45; postmentum length 1.25, 1.25; maximum width of the postmentum 0.35, 0.35; minimum width of the postmentum 0.17, 0.17; pronotum length 0.50, 0.47; pronotum width 1.07, 1.05.
